name: Cloud with Rain
tldr: 🌧️ shows rain or gloomy weather, and jokingly suggests sadness, tears, disappointment, or a dreary mood.

contextMeanings.meaning: It refers to rain, wet conditions, or weather that is about to become wet.
contextMeanings.example: bring an umbrella, it’s already 🌧️ outside

contextMeanings.meaning: It acts as a quick way to say that someone feels sad, overwhelmed, or stuck in a bad mood.
contextMeanings.example: my commute was so long today 🌧️

contextMeanings.meaning: It can exaggerate a minor annoyance as though it were a full personal downpour.
contextMeanings.example: one canceled meeting and now my whole week feels 🌧️

contextMeanings.meaning: It can invite comfort or gently say that the conversation has a melancholy, disappointed, or emotionally heavy feeling.
contextMeanings.example: i was really hoping we could meet tonight 🌧️

platformNotes.note: In a close conversation, 🌧️ often works as a quick emotional aside after a complaint or disappointment. Adding “it’s literally raining here” can make the literal meaning clear.
In captions and story replies, 🌧️ can underline a sad, reflective, or hopeless mood. It also remains useful when the weather itself is the subject of a photo or update.
On TikTok, people often place 🌧️ beside a complaint, bad update, or sad song to make the mood immediately visible. The emoji does not need a long explanation in that setting.
In WhatsApp chats, 🌧️ is usually a compact response to bad news, plans falling through, or someone saying they feel low. Nearby words can distinguish sadness from joking exaggeration.

generationalNotes.note: Gen Z commonly uses 🌧️ as playful shorthand for tears, sadness, or emotional exhaustion. Its exaggerated tone can make a complaint feel lighter than a serious disclosure.
Millennials tend to read 🌧️ as both literal bad weather and a visual way to describe a miserable mood. The surrounding sentence usually determines the intended meaning.
Gen X may take 🌧️ more literally in a weather discussion or when plans involve going outside. They still use it for gloom, but clearer wording carries more weight.

warnings.title: Sadness or actual rain?
warnings.description: A message about someone feeling devastated can be misread as a joke about bad weather. Add “i’m actually a bit sad” or “it’s really pouring here” instead of relying on 🌧️ alone.

warnings.title: Pain can become trivial
warnings.description: 🌧️ can make tears or disappointment sound playful and exaggerated. When someone shares grief, serious illness, or another painful experience, use words and a clearly sympathetic response.

seoDescription: What does 🌧️ mean? It shows rainy or gloomy conditions, and people use it to signal sadness, tears, disappointment, or a dreary mood.

longForm.overview:
🌧️ is the Cloud with Rain emoji, so its plain meaning is wet, grey, rainy weather. That is why it appears in messages about a washed-out commute, a ruined picnic, or a forecast that turned plans upside down. It can also stand for a miserable mood without spelling out the feeling: “my plans are dead 🌧️” reads as a small dramatic complaint rather than a weather report.

The emoji separates itself from ☔, which usually focuses on an umbrella or one person in the rain, and from ☁️, which can suggest an overcast sky without falling drops. 🌧️ gives the image an active, unpleasant feeling. People use it when they want to say “the day is dragging me down,” “this is depressing,” or “I’m having a cry.” In a joke, one emoji can replace a paragraph about being upset. In a serious exchange, however, the same picture may feel too cute or indirect for the emotion being described. The words beside it matter: literal rain, tired disappointment, and genuine sadness need different company.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
The moment that prompts 🌧️ is usually a small defeat: plans fall through, the forecast ruins an outing, traffic crawls, or news leaves someone feeling low. Friends send it after saying they had a terrible day, often in a sentence such as “the rain caught me at every turn 🌧️.” It works as punctuation for a mood, especially when the sender wants sympathy without sounding too formal.

It can also arrive as a joke before the explanation. Someone might post 🌧️ beside a photo of an umbrella turned inside out or describe a canceled trip as “the sky matched my mood.” In conversation, it often means “I’m blue,” “this is getting to me,” or “everything is going wrong today.” Used alone, it leaves the exact feeling open, so the next message usually supplies the joke or complaint.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Avoid 🌧️ when someone is describing serious grief, trauma, illness, or a crisis. The teardrop imagery can make the pain sound decorative or lightly funny, especially if the sender has been using the emoji for exaggerated complaints. A straightforward sentence and a caring response are better than a weather picture in that moment.

It can also misfire when the sender means literal rain. Older relatives or people discussing an outdoor event may take 🌧️ as a factual comment about conditions rather than a mood. Add “just the weather” or name the feeling directly. Likewise, do not use it as a response to serious vulnerability unless the conversation has already established a playful tone. ☁️ may fit a general grey outlook better, while 😭 can more clearly suggest tears, but neither replaces empathy.
longForm.howToReply:
If the 🌧️ was a complaint, match its weather language first: “sounds like a rough commute,” “the sky really committed to the bit,” or “i’ll send you dry socks if you’re soaked.” For a playful exchange, describe the imaginary storm, but make the joke fit the relationship.

If the emoji landed on your own bad news, ask whether it means the literal weather or how you feel. A reply such as “still raining, or are you actually sad?” clears up the ambiguity without dismissing either possibility. When someone sends 🌧️ with a complaint, offering practical help—changing plans, providing a ride, or simply listening—usually works better than another sad face. If the message seems serious, drop the weather joke and acknowledge the feeling directly.

faqs.question: What does 🌧️ mean from a guy?
faqs.answer: 🌧️ usually says he feels gloomy, disappointed, or a little dramatic about the situation. It can also mean the weather is genuinely bad, so the words around it determine the intended meaning.

faqs.question: Is 🌧️ flirty?
faqs.answer: 🌧️ is not inherently flirty. In a dating chat, it can soften a disappointed or sad message, but it is more often a reaction to the mood or circumstances than a romantic signal.

faqs.question: What does 🌧️ mean on TikTok?
faqs.answer: On TikTok, 🌧️ commonly underlines sadness, emotional exhaustion, bad luck, or a miserable situation. It is often used beside a complaint, a dramatic update, or a sad sound.

faqs.question: Does 🌧️ mean someone is crying?
faqs.answer: It can suggest tears, but it more broadly suggests a sad or gloomy mood. If someone wants to communicate serious crying, they will usually add words that make that clear.

conversationExamples.message: my flight got delayed again and it’s already 🌧️ here
conversationExamples.interpretation: They are mixing genuine travel frustration with literal rainy weather. Respond with sympathy or a funny weather complaint rather than assuming they need emotional support.

conversationExamples.message: i was really hoping we could meet tonight, but the weather turned 🌧️
conversationExamples.interpretation: They may be disappointed about a canceled plan, though the emoji also leaves room for a playful explanation. Acknowledge the lost evening and suggest another time.

conversationExamples.message: the client moved the meeting three times and now my whole afternoon feels 🌧️
conversationExamples.interpretation: They are exaggerating their frustration in a playful way. Ask what happened or offer a quick distraction, but keep the response light if this is meant as banter.

conversationExamples.message: it’s really pouring here 🌧️ so i’ll pick up groceries on the way home
conversationExamples.interpretation: Here 🌧️ is mostly literal and explains a practical change in plans. Respond to the errand or offer to help rather than treating it as a sadness signal.

conversationExamples.message: group chat has been dead for three days and my mood is fully 🌧️
conversationExamples.interpretation: They are joking that the inactive chat makes them gloomy. Send a lively message, revive the group, or acknowledge the exaggerated sadness without making it heavy.
